requirements.evidence: Migrations match the spec: entities slug unique 'entities_slug_unique' + softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:16-21); memberships FKs cascadeOnDelete, role default 'employee', storedAs owner_seq "case when role = 'owner' then 1 else null end", unique indexes 'entity_memberships_entity_user_unique' and 'entity_memberships_one_owner' (create_entity_memberships_table.php:12-31). Entity has HasFactory/SoftDeletes, getRouteKeyName()='slug', memberships(), users(), owner() HasOne filtered on Owner (Entity.php:18-55). EntityMembership enum cast, owner/admin/employee scopes, entity()/user() (EntityMembership.php). UserRole enum with manageable() [Admin, Employee] (UserRole.php:5-19). User::memberships/entities/membershipFor(int) (User.php:34-60). Factories with owner/admin/employee states. Both policies implement the stated rules, incl. owner membership never deletable and self-removal (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:31-42).

conventions.evidence: Authorization via policies in app/Policies; $fillable set deliberately with #[Fillable] attribute matching User.php style; reversible down() in both migrations; docs/database-schema.md updated to replace owner_membership_id with the owner_seq design (database-schema.md:596) plus CHANGELOG under Unreleased and docs/README.md. Minor: the ER diagram also drops the proposed 'string locale_default' column, which is unrelated to the owner_membership_id replacement.

security.evidence: Policies default to deny for non-members (membershipFor(...)?->role with strict in_array), manageSettings owner-only, owner membership never deletable; fillable lists are explicit. Gap: assignRole (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:22-25) lets an admin target the owner's membership (or their own), so a future role-assignment action relying only on this ability could let an admin demote the owner; the task does not explicitly forbid it, so impact is limited for now.

tests.evidence: Three Pest files cover schema columns, named indexes, slug uniqueness, soft deletes, route key, factories/states, DB role default, scopes, (entity,user) uniqueness, second-owner rejection on insert and on promotion, multiple owners across entities, relations, cascades, enum, and every policy ability with allowed and denied (employee, outsider, non-member) cases plus gate discovery. Only quibble: index test uses SQLite-only 'PRAGMA index_list' (EntityDataModelTest.php:39-41).

simplicity.evidence: Lean models and policies; DB-level constraint instead of app logic. Small duplication: identical private manages() helper in EntityPolicy.php:52-59 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:44-51.

readability.evidence: Clear names, short methods with PHPDoc describing each rule (e.g. EntityMembershipPolicy.php:27-30), explanatory comment on owner_seq in the migration (create_entity_memberships_table.php:23-24); no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Only models, migrations, factories, policies, tests and the docs/CHANGELOG the task asked to update; no routes, session, pages or translations. The removal of locale_default from the proposal doc is the only edit beyond the task.

issues.explanation: assignRole returns true for any owner/admin regardless of the target, so an admin is authorized to change the owner's membership role (or their own), which could let an admin demote the owner once an action uses this ability.
The index-name test queries 'PRAGMA index_list', which only works on SQLite, so it would fail if the suite runs against MariaDB even though the task requires portability across both.
The ER diagram also drops the proposed 'locale_default' column on entities, which is unrelated to replacing owner_membership_id and silently loses a design note.
The private manages() helper is duplicated verbatim in both policies; a small shared helper (e.g. on EntityMembership/UserRole) would avoid the copy.

review.summary: Adds the entities and entity_memberships tables with a portable generated-column single-owner constraint, the Entity/EntityMembership models, UserRole enum, factories, both policies, thorough Pest tests and the requested doc updates. Requirements and contract are fully met with good test coverage; only minor points remain (assignRole can target the owner membership, a SQLite-only index test, a small doc deletion and duplicated helper), so it is approvable with nits.
